wtp_streams.question: What do Indian institutional buyers actually pay for software like this?
wtp_streams.method: Read live vendor price pages for Indian incubation and campus software.
wtp_streams.evidence: Fedena ₹50k/₹75k/₹1L for a FULL ERP with unlimited users; NestLens Orbit ₹75k-₹2.5L; IncubatX ₹1.2L-₹7.2L.

wtp_streams.question: What is the cheapest way for a buyer to say no to us?
wtp_streams.method: Identify zero-cost substitutes a buyer can adopt instead.
wtp_streams.evidence: Univation's Incubators Platform is offered FREE to universities and nonprofits. Founderhood has a free tier. Founderhood also publishes a 15% university/nonprofit discount off list.
wtp_streams.direction: sets the floor and destroys margin at the low end

wtp_streams.question: At what price does the buying process change behaviour?
wtp_streams.method: Phase 2 committee-trigger analysis across 8 institutional instruments.
wtp_streams.evidence: Committee-trigger spread is Rs 50,000 to Rs 10,00,000 across the instruments reviewed in Phase 2. Below ~Rs 50k a purchase is routine; above it, a committee is convened, which lengthens the cycle and raises CAC - which is exactly the constraint we are trying to relieve.
wtp_streams.direction: high ACV is self-defeating on sales-cycle grounds

wtp_streams.question: What happens if we sell through GeM or a state tender?
wtp_streams.method: Published GeM procurement-mode bands and observed bid dispersion.
wtp_streams.evidence: GeM L1 band is INR 25,000-5,00,000. Bid and Reverse Auction is MANDATORY at INR 5,00,000+. Observed L1-L5 spread for services is 5-15%, and in 60-70% of tenders L1 lands below the buyer's estimate.
wtp_streams.direction: caps realised price when selling to government

wtp_streams.question: What is the pain actually worth?
wtp_streams.method: Cost-of-failure anchor from the Phase 1 problem corpus.
wtp_streams.evidence: P-A07 (patent deadline tracking absent) is the only CRITICAL finding in the Phase 1 corpus. A single missed NIRF/NAAC deadline or a lost grant cycle costs far more than an annual subscription, which is why value-based pricing can exceed comparables - but only where the buyer feels the pain directly.
wtp_streams.direction: the only stream that can justify a premium

wtp_streams.question: Is our scope bigger or smaller than what buyers can get for less?
wtp_streams.method: Feature-breadth comparison against the cheapest broad competitor.
wtp_streams.evidence: Fedena sells admissions, attendance, exams, fees, library, hostel, transport, payroll, parent portal and mobile apps - strictly MORE than StartupHub - at Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per institution per year with unlimited users. Any price above Rs 1 lakh must be justified on scope, and scope is the one axis where we currently lose.
wtp_streams.direction: the binding constraint on the list price

frames.read: Our list price of Rs 1.2L is ALREADY 20% above this ceiling. Competing here at Rs 1.2L means being more expensive than a strictly broader product.

frames.read: Under this frame Rs 1.2L is comfortable and Scenario B's Rs 10.28L is still 1.43x above everything observed.

binding_frame.ceiling_basis: Fedena Ultimate, full ERP, unlimited users
binding_frame.read: Our list price of Rs 1.2L is ALREADY 20% above this ceiling. Competing here at Rs 1.2L means being more expensive than a strictly broader product.

wtp_bracket.note: Floor is Rs 50,000 - below that we are under market and cannot fund CAC. The ceiling is frame-dependent, so it is published per frame rather than collapsed. Against the binding frame (campus ERP) our list price is already 1.2x the ceiling.

wtp_framing.finding: The ceiling depends entirely on WHICH competitor set the buyer accepts. Judged against campus ERPs, we are capped near Rs 1 lakh. Judged against incubation platforms, Rs 7.2 lakh is defensible. Judged on cost-of-failure, Rs 6 lakh is arguable. These are three different answers to three different questions, and averaging them produces a number that answers none.
wtp_framing.consequence: The real pricing decision is not 'what is the market willing to pay' but 'which competitor are we actually up against at renewal'. That is a sales-positioning choice, not a research finding, which is why it must be stated rather than modelled.

models.name: Flat Rs 2-5 lakh/year

models.why: Defensible only against direct incubation-platform competitors, and it crosses the GeM ₹5 lakh reverse-auction threshold at the top of the band.

models.name: Per-user pricing
models.why: Institutions cap the seats that touch innovation data at a handful (Phase 2 found 25 roles, only 4 with documented budget authority). Per-user pricing would collapse ACV to a few thousand rupees. Note Zoho requires a 25-licence minimum for Lite seats - the same trap.

models.name: Institution + number of startups
models.mechanic: platform fee plus a fee per incubated startup tracked
models.where_on_ladder: matches how IncubatX and NestLens actually scale
models.comparable: IncubatX 'up to 4 cohorts'; NestLens 'scales with cohort size'
models.why: Aligns price with the thing the institution is actually measured on - the cohort. Directly parallels the SISFS scheme, which pays incubators 5% management fee on the grant value they administer.

models.name: Base platform + premium modules
models.mechanic: core subscription plus paid add-on modules
models.where_on_ladder: proven - IncubatX Media Kit ₹15k/mo; incuTrack add-ons
models.comparable: IncubatX Media Kit add-on; incuTrack Mentor Matching/Surveys/Events
models.why: Lets us enter low (Model A/B) and expand with the buyer instead of front-loading the whole price at the first committee meeting.

per_user_failure.note: Phase 2 found 25 roles touching innovation data and only 4 with documented budget authority. At Zoho's published per-user rates, a 5-10 seat deployment pays Rs 48,000-3,12,000 a year - below the flat list price, and with no floor because Zoho itself imposes a 25-licence minimum on Lite seats.

wtp_instrument.name: Institutional WTP instrument - Van Westendorp + Gabor-Granger
wtp_instrument.why: Van Westendorp yields an acceptable price interval and Gabor-Granger yields a demand curve. Both require asking buyers. Neither can be simulated into legitimacy, so no results are published.

van_westendorp.text: What is the least you would be willing to pay per year for a system that produced a defensible innovation report without manual assembly?
At what price would you consider the purchase too expensive to justify to your finance office?
At what price would you begin to seriously consider it?
At what price would it feel cheap - that you would be delighted to have budget for it?

wtp_instrument.ladder_basis: Anchored on the observed Indian envelope (Rs 50k-7.2L) and straddling both Phase 7 scenarios (Rs 1.2L and Rs 10.28L).

probing_questions.text: Who else would have to approve this budget line, and what is their threshold for convening a committee?
What does your institution spend today on this - including staff time - even if the answer is zero rupees of software?
probing_questions.measures: revealed current spend, the real substitute price

probing_questions.text: If you lost your current manual process tomorrow, what would that cost you in a missed deadline or a lost grant?
Would you pay more if the system also produced your NIRF and NAAC submission artefacts automatically?
probing_questions.measures: premium headroom for Model F modules

wtp_instrument.coding_note: Reuse the Phase 3B protocol, consent form and coding scheme. Do not create a parallel interview regime.
